* Shaykh: No, it came before, and we said to you: ﴿Have you not seen that Allah sends down water from the sky, and the earth becomes green?﴾ [al-Hajj 63]. We said: Zayd married and then a child was born to him, and that the sequence (ta'qib) is according to its nature: the sequence of each thing is according to what suits it. And that it does not follow from His saying ﴿when they are reminded of them, they fall down﴾ that they fall down from the moment of reminder. We forgot to say this during the discussion. So the meaning of ﴿when they are reminded of them, they fall down in prostration﴾ is that they prostrate to Allah and glorify Him while in prostration. For this reason, among what is prescribed in prostration is that you say: "Glory be to You, O Allah, our Lord, and praise be to You."
Allah the Exalted says: ﴿So taste [the punishment] because you forgot the meeting of this your Day﴾ up to the end [al-Sajdah 14].
* From this noble verse it is derived: the people of the Fire are reproached for abandoning action that would save them from it, by His saying: ﴿So taste because you forgot the meeting of this your Day﴾. From this benefit follows an increase in punishment. Is it physical or spiritual punishment? Spiritual, because when a person is rebuked for a deed he did, he increases in regret and remorse.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the use of forgetting to mean abandoning, by His saying: ﴿you forgot﴾, and ﴿We have forgotten you﴾.
* Among its benefits: the affirmation of Allah's voluntary acts, the Exalted. From where? ﴿We have forgotten you﴾, that is, We have abandoned you, and this indicates that He abandons whom He wills and turns to whom He wills.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the punishment of the Fire is permissible, by His saying: ﴿and taste the punishment of eternity﴾. This is what Ahl al-Sunnah wa al-Jama'ah hold: the punishment of the Fire is everlasting and eternal, just as the bliss of Paradise is everlasting and eternal. But Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him, mentioned that the early scholars had two opinions regarding the everlastingness of the Fire. As for its punishment, it is everlasting as long as the Fire exists, so its people will never leave it while it exists. But the discussion concerns the Fire's own everlastingness: is it eternal (mu'abbadah) or lasting for a long period (mu'ammadah)? The correct view is that it is eternal. Allah the Exalted has mentioned this in three verses of the Quran: in Surat al-Nisa', in Surat al-Ahzab, and in Surat al-Jinn. In Surat al-Nisa', give us the verse.
* Student: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved and wronged, Allah would never forgive them nor guide them﴾ [al-Nisa' 168].
* Shaykh: ﴿Nor guide them﴾ [al-Nisa' 168].
* Student: To a path.
* Shaykh: ﴿A path, except the path of Hell, to abide therein forever. And that is ever easy for Allah﴾ [al-Nisa' 168–169]. That is the verse of al-Nisa'. The second is in al-Ahzab...
Student: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved in Our signs﴾ [al-Nisa' 56].
* Shaykh: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved and wronged﴾.
* Student: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved and wronged, Allah would never forgive them﴾.
* Shaykh: ﴿Nor guide them﴾.
* Student: To a path.
* Shaykh: ﴿A path, except the path of Hell, to abide therein forever. And that is ever easy for Allah﴾ [al-Nisa' 168–169]. That is the verse of al-Nisa'. The second in al-Ahzab, what is the verse of al-Ahzab?
* Student: ﴿to abide therein forever; they will find no protector or helper﴾ [al-Ahzab 65].
* Shaykh: It is in the verse of al-Jinn.
* Student: ﴿And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger, then indeed for him is the fire of Hell, abiding therein forever﴾ [al-Jinn 23].
* Shaykh: ﴿Then indeed for him is the fire of Hell, abiding therein forever﴾.
If someone says: the eternity mentioned here refers only to their abiding (khulud)?
We say: there is no abiding unless the place in which one abides is eternal. When abiding is made eternal, the place of abiding is necessarily eternal. For this reason, the correct and definite view is that the Fire is eternal.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: Allah the Exalted does not wrong anyone, by His saying: ﴿because of what you used to do﴾ [al-Sajdah 14].
* Among its benefits: recompense is of the same kind as the deed. Just as they spent their lives in disobedience to Allah, their life in the Hereafter will also be in the punishment of Allah.
Then Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Only those believe in Our signs who, when they are reminded of them, fall down in prostration and exalt the praise of their Lord, and they are not arrogant﴾ [al-Sajdah 15].
* From this noble verse it is derived: faith has signs, by His saying: ﴿Only those believe in Our signs who, when they are reminded of them﴾, and so on.
* And from it: whoever claims faith without its sign, his claim is invalid.
* And from the noble verse: the use of circumstances and indicators as evidence. From where is it derived? Because Allah mentioned a sign of faith in these actions, and faith's place is the heart, which is not known. But these deeds are indicators and circumstances that point to the existence of what they are evidence for. So the verse indicates the use of indicators as evidence. What else? And circumstances point to the reality of a thing. This is extremely beneficial for judges.
Among the noble prophets, one used indicators as evidence. Who? Sulayman. He used indicators as evidence. The Prophet ﷺ also used indicators as evidence in the case of the wealth of Huyayy ibn Akhtab, when he was asked about it after Khaybar. He said: "It was consumed by the wars." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The wealth is much, and the covenant is recent." It was not possible for it to be finished, and Huyayy ibn Akhtab was one of the wealthy men of Banu al-Nadir. Where did his wealth go? Then he gave him to al-Zubayr ibn al-'Awwam and said to him: "Torture him." When he beat him, he said: "By Allah, I will show you something Huyayy used to frequent often." So he showed them a ruin, and there the wealth was buried in it.[[Ibn Hibban (1697) narrated from Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to the uncle of Huyayy: "... What became of the treasure of Huyayy which he brought from al-Nadir?" He said: "It was consumed by expenses and wars." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The covenant is recent, and the wealth is more than that." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave him to al-Zubayr, and he tortured him. Huyayy had previously entered a ruin, and he said: "I saw Huyayy going around in a ruin here." So they went and searched, and they found the treasure in the ruin... The hadith.]] So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used indicators to establish the existence of the thing.
* From the noble verse: faith has completeness and deficiency, because this verse is undoubtedly about the completeness of faith.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the believer's submission to admonitions. Among the signs of the believer is his submission to admonitions, by His saying: ﴿who, when they are reminded of them﴾ [al-Sajdah 15].
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: a believing person may be affected by ignorance and forgetfulness. From where is it derived? ﴿When they are reminded of them﴾: they may forget or be ignorant.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the obligation of prostration, by His saying: ﴿they fall down in prostration﴾ [al-Sajdah 15]. It has been established in the hadith that: "The closest a servant is to his Lord is when he is prostrating." The Prophet ﷺ commanded striving in supplication during prostration, and informed that it is more likely to be answered.[[Narrated by Muslim (482/215) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]] [[Narrated by 'Abd al-Razzaq (2839) from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: "I was forbidden to recite in bowing and prostration. As for bowing, the Lord is glorified therein; as for prostration, strive therein in supplication, for it is worthy that you be answered."]]

* One of the benefits of this noble verse: combining the negation of defects and deficiency from Allah with the affirmation of His perfection. From where do we derive this? ﴿And glorify the praise of their Lord﴾ [As-Sajdah 15]. In "tasbih" (glorifying Allah by declaring Him free of imperfection) there is transcendence, and in "hamd" (praise) there is perfection.

* One of the benefits of this noble verse: humility is one of the attributes of the believer, based on His saying: ﴿and they are not arrogant﴾. Humility toward whom? Toward the truth and toward creation. But we must know the difference between humility (tawadu') and abasement (dhull). The believer is not abased, but he is humble. When the truth becomes clear to him, he submits to it; this is humility before the truth. And when he deals with people, he deals with them with humility, but he does not debase himself. He is not arrogant toward people, and he does not deny people their rights, but he does not demean himself before them.

* It is derived from this noble verse that blind adherence to tradition (ta'assub fi al-taqlid) is not the way of the believers, based on His saying: ﴿and they are not arrogant﴾. Among those who are fanatically attached to blind imitation are those who are arrogant toward the truth. When it is presented to them, they refuse, and they dismiss it by saying, "So-and-so, one of the imitated scholars, said such-and-such." This is a form of arrogance toward the truth.

* It is also derived from this noble verse: the censure of one who insists on his opinion despite its falsehood. From where is this derived?
* Student: ﴿and they are not arrogant﴾.
* Shaykh: ﴿and they are not arrogant﴾. Some people, when they say a statement, cannot possibly retract it even when the truth has become evident. This is a type of arrogance. It is obligatory that you know yourself, that you are a human being, and that knowledge may escape you either through forgetfulness or ignorance, and that you may also fail to reach the goal. You may have knowledge, but lack focus, reflection, the combining of evidences, and similar things, so you need to be reminded.

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Their sides forsake their beds﴾ [As-Sajdah 16], to the end.

* From this verse is derived the virtue of the night prayer (qiyam al-layl), because Allah, exalted is He, mentioned it in the context of negation: ﴿Their sides forsake their beds﴾. But this general expression is restricted by what? By what the Sunnah has brought, meaning that one should not stay awake the entire night. ﴿Their sides forsake their beds﴾ is within the limits of what the Sunnah has brought. By this we recognize the error found in books of exhortation, which say that so-and-so prayed the Fajr prayer with the ablution of 'Isha' for forty years, meaning that he never slept at night and stood in prayer all night. This is an error, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) disavowed it. When a group of people said, one of them saying, "I pray all night and do not sleep," he said: "As for me, I pray and I sleep. Whoever turns away from my Sunnah is not of me."[[Reported by al-Bukhari (5063), and Muslim, with his wording (1401/5), from Anas (may Allah be pleased with him), that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "...What is the matter with people who say such-and-such? But I pray and I sleep, I fast and I break my fast, and I marry women. Whoever turns away from my Sunnah is not of me."]]

But the problem with those preachers who write these books is that they want to encourage people, but they encourage them toward falsehood. If people were only given what is authentically reported from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) of glad tidings and warnings, and of righteous deeds, they would have been upright. But when I hear that a man is praised because for forty years he prayed Fajr with the ablution of 'Isha', I say: where am I in comparison with this? I will remain as I am. I pray the two Sunnah rak'ahs after 'Isha', and the minimum of Witr is one rak'ah, which I pray. Only the recitation of al-Fatihah is obligatory, and I limit myself to al-Fatihah. Only "Subhana Rabbiyal-A'la" once in prostration is obligatory, and "Subhana Rabbiyal-'Azim" once in bowing, and I limit myself to these as well, and I proceed. But if people were truly shown the Sunnah, it would suffice them as obligatory.

* One of the benefits of this noble verse: the virtue of supplication, based on His saying: ﴿They call upon their Lord﴾.

* And among its benefits: it is fitting for the one who supplicates and for the one who worships, and also for the worshipper who acts, that his supplication and worship be between fear and hope, based on His saying: ﴿in fear and in hope﴾.

* One of the benefits of this noble verse: the virtue of spending from what Allah has provided you, based on His saying: ﴿and from what We have provided them they spend﴾ [As-Sajdah 16], according to the detail we mentioned in the tafsir.

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for their eyes as a reward for what they used to do﴾ [As-Sajdah 17]. In this verse is evidence of the greatness of the bliss of Paradise. From where is this derived? From His saying: ﴿No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for their eyes﴾, because there is no doubt that this indefiniteness indicates magnification, as we said in the tafsir.

* One of the benefits of this noble verse: that in Paradise there is comfort for the eyes in food, clothing, drink, and dwelling that does not occur to the mind, because all four of these bring comfort to the eye. The poet said:
"The wearing of a coarse woolen cloak, and the comfort of my eye,
are dearer to me than wearing fine silk."

* One of the benefits of this noble verse: the grace of Allah, mighty and majestic, upon His servants, upon the believers. His grace is both prior and subsequent. The prior grace is that He granted them success in faith and righteous deeds. The subsequent grace is that He made this a reward for their deeds: ﴿as a reward for what they used to do﴾. It is as if these blessings in Paradise were a reward for deeds they performed. So there is in it the reality of their work, but there is also in it the grace of Allah, mighty and majestic, upon them, as if it were a grace from them upon themselves.

His saying: ﴿as a reward for what they used to do﴾ is like His saying: ﴿Is the reward for good anything but good?﴾ [Ar-Rahman 60], the goodness of the deed being rewarded with the goodness of the recompense. And like His saying: ﴿Indeed, this has been for you a reward, and your effort has been appreciated﴾ [Al-Insan 22]. He bestows upon them the praiseworthy striving and then thanks them for it. Here He bestows upon them the granting of success in guidance, then says: I will reward you for your deeds. There is no doubt that this is part of the completeness of the favor of Allah, mighty and majestic.

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Is one who was a believer like one who was defiantly disobedient? They are not equal﴾ [As-Sajdah 18].

* In this verse is an affirmation that there is no equality between the believer and whom? The disbeliever. This is something impossible. ﴿Is one who was a believer like one who was defiantly disobedient?﴾ Allah, exalted is He, said in another verse: ﴿Then shall We treat the Muslims like the criminals? What is wrong with you? How do you judge?﴾ [Al-Qalam 35-36]. This is foolishness and an error in judgment, to make the Muslim like the criminal or the defiantly disobedient like the believer: ﴿Is one who was a believer like one who was defiantly disobedient?﴾

* One of the benefits of this noble verse: the believer is better than the defiantly disobedient, even if the disobedient one has greater standing in this world among people. From where is this derived? From generality: ﴿Is one who﴾ — "man" here is an interrogative noun, and interrogative nouns are among the forms of generality. It is impossible for any defiantly disobedient person to be like the believer, even if the world magnifies him and even if he attains from the world whatever he attains. He is not like the believer: ﴿They are not equal﴾.

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, they will have the Gardens of refuge as hospitality for what they used to do. But as for those who defied, their refuge is the Fire﴾ [As-Sajdah 19-20].

* It is derived from this noble verse that the believer is not equal to the disbeliever, neither in deed nor in recompense. As for deed, it is evident: this one is a believer and this one is defiantly disobedient. As for recompense, Allah has clarified the difference: those who believed and did righteous deeds have the Gardens of refuge, and those have the Fire as their refuge, and He distinguished between this and that.

* One of the benefits of this noble verse: faith is not complete except with righteous deeds, based on His saying: ﴿As for those who believed and did righteous deeds﴾. So mere belief is not sufficient; there must be righteous deeds.

* It is derived from this noble verse: the affirmation of Paradise, based on His saying: ﴿they will have the Gardens of refuge﴾. But does it exist now, or will it come into being on the Day of Resurrection? It exists now, based on His saying: ﴿It has been prepared for the righteous﴾ [Al 'Imran 133], and "prepared" is a past-tense verb.

* One of the benefits of this noble verse: the goodness of the dwellings and abodes of Paradise, based on His saying: ﴿they will have the Gardens of refuge﴾, meaning the gardens to which a person wishes only to retreat for refuge. Everyone wishes for this refuge, but only those who believed and did righteous deeds attain it.

* One of the benefits of this noble verse: the people of Paradise are honored with the blessings with which they are given delight, just as a guest is honored with hospitality. You know what a guest feels in his soul when he is honored with hospitality, unlike one to whom food is served in the ordinary way, who sees it as something routine and of no importance. But one who is served as a guest, as though he were an honored and respected man, finds in himself, along with the physical pleasure of the food, a pleasure, psychological ease, and honor. For this reason Allah, exalted is He, named it ﴿hospitality﴾ (nuzul).

* One of the benefits of this noble verse: the recompense is of the same kind as the deed, based on His saying: ﴿as hospitality for what they used to do﴾.

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿But as for those who defied﴾, to the end.

* It is derived from this noble verse that defiance (fisq) is of two kinds: greater defiance, which is disbelief, and lesser defiance, which is sin.

* And among its benefits: the disbelievers' refuge is the Fire, based on His saying: ﴿But as for those who defied, their refuge is the Fire﴾.

There is another kind of defiance that does not remove one from the religion, such as His saying: ﴿And do not insult one another by nicknames. Wretched is the name of defiance after faith﴾ [Al-Hujurat 11]. Here He said ﴿their refuge is the Fire﴾, and He did not say "for them is the Fire as a refuge," or "for them is the Fire of refuge." The difference is that no one loves the Fire to be his refuge, unlike the first verse, where everyone loves Paradise to be the refuge, but not this. Although this distinction may vary in some verses, such as: ﴿But as for one who transgressed and preferred the worldly life, indeed, Hellfire will be the refuge. And as for one who feared the standing before his Lord and restrained the soul from [its] desire, Paradise will be the refuge﴾ [An-Nazi'at 37-41]. But each context has its own speech. Here the context is one of equivalence and comparison, and for this reason He distinguished between the two. He said ﴿Gardens of refuge﴾ and here He said ﴿their refuge is the Fire﴾. There, however, there is no equivalence, meaning that it was not mentioned that a people claim for themselves that they are the people of truth, so Allah denied that.

* One of the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of the Fire, based on His saying: ﴿their refuge is the Fire﴾. Does it exist now, or will it come into being on the Day of Resurrection? It exists now. The evidence: ﴿It has been prepared for the disbelievers﴾ [Al-Baqarah 24].

* One of the benefits of this noble verse: the severity of the punishment of the people of the Fire, because they are given hope of coming out and are lifted up; the flame rises with them, until when they think they are about to come out, they are returned into it, based on His saying: ﴿Every time they wish to get out of it from distress, they are returned into it﴾ [Al-Hajj 22].

* And among the benefits of this noble verse also: the people of the Fire are made to suffer both physical punishment and inner punishment through reproach, ﴿And it will be said to them: Taste the punishment of the Fire, which you used to deny﴾ [As-Sajdah 20].

Then Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And We will surely let them taste from the nearer punishment short of the greater punishment; perhaps they will return﴾ [As-Sajdah 21].

* It is derived from this noble verse: the explanation of (...) Allah, mighty and majestic, regarding what He tests with calamities. From where is this derived? From His saying: ﴿And We will surely let them taste﴾ and ﴿perhaps they will return﴾. This is like His saying: ﴿Corruption has appeared on the land and sea by [reason of] what the hands of people have earned, so He may let them taste part of that which they have done that perhaps they will return﴾ [Ar-Rum 41].

* One of the benefits of this noble verse: the punishment of this world is not to be compared with the punishment of the Hereafter, because of the great difference between them. This is nearer and that is greater; both are at opposite extremes. "Nearer" is a comparative form, and "greater" is a comparative form. So can the nearest thing be compared to the highest thing? No, there is no comparison. For this reason you say (...) the great difference between the punishment of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter.

* It is derived from this noble verse: the acceptance of repentance from a disbeliever, based on His saying: ﴿perhaps they will return﴾.

* It is derived from this noble verse: the affirmation of Allah's wisdom, based on His saying: ﴿perhaps they will return﴾, for "perhaps" (la'alla) indicates causation, and causation is wisdom.

* And among the benefits of this noble verse also: the affirmation of punishment in the Hereafter, based on His saying: ﴿short of the greater punishment﴾, for by it is meant the punishment of the Hereafter.

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And who is more unjust than one who is reminded of the verses of his Lord and then turns away from them?﴾ [As-Sajdah 22], to the end.

* It is derived from this noble verse that whoever is of this description, no one is more unjust than him, based on His saying: ﴿And who is more unjust﴾. Here there is an issue: this expression has come in reference to others as well. Allah said: ﴿And who is more unjust than one who prevents the mosques of Allah from having His name mentioned therein﴾ [Al-Baqarah 114], and ﴿And who is more unjust than one who invents about Allah a lie﴾ [Al-An'am 21]. Here we need to reconcile these texts. In the Sunnah: "And who is more unjust than one who sets out to create like My creation?"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (7559), Muslim (2111/101), from Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him).]] So how do we reconcile these texts?

We mentioned previously that reconciliation is done in one of two ways. The first way is to say: the verse ﴿And who is more unjust﴾ does not indicate that there is no one who shares or equals this injustice. We say: "And who is more unjust than..." — both share in the highest degree of injustice, this is one way. The second way is to say: the "more unjust" is relative to what is below it within its own category. That is, ﴿And who is more unjust than one who is reminded of the verses of his Lord and then turns away from them﴾: this is the most unjust of those who are admonished, unlike one who is admonished and then turns away from only part of them, or something similar. Here the greater injustice is in relation to what is below it in its own category. ﴿And who is more unjust than one who prevents the mosques of Allah﴾: meaning no one is more unjust in preventing anything than one who prevents the mosques of Allah. Based on this, compare. So the answer becomes one of two ways: either it is said (...).

* The noble verse: the obligation to accept admonition for one who is reminded of the verses of Allah. From where do we derive this?
* Student: From the threat concerning turning away.
* Shaykh: Yes, from the threat concerning turning away.

* And among the benefits of this noble verse: that a person must accept admonition from whomever admonishes him. From where do we derive this?
* Student: From the passive voice.
* Shaykh: From the construction of the verb in the passive voice: ﴿is reminded﴾. He did not say "from one whom the Messenger reminded, or whom so-and-so reminded." If admonition occurs, or if admonition reaches you from any source, it is obligatory upon you to accept it.

* And among the benefits of this noble verse: turning away after knowledge is uglier than turning away in a state of ignorance, or not? Because Allah, exalted is He, made this the greatest injustice: that you be reminded and then turn away. But whoever turns away without being reminded is less culpable.

* And among the benefits of this noble verse: the recompense is of the same kind as the deed, based on His saying: ﴿Indeed, We will take retribution upon the criminals﴾ [As-Sajdah 22].

* And among its benefits: turning away from the signs of Allah after being reminded of them is criminality, based on His saying: ﴿Indeed, We are of the criminals﴾.

* And among the benefits of this noble verse: the permissibility of attributing retribution to Allah in a restricted way, based on His saying: ﴿Indeed, We will take retribution upon the criminals﴾. That is, the report about Allah that He takes retribution, but restricted, like His saying: ﴿Indeed, We are of the criminals, taking retribution﴾.

* And among its benefits: the affirmation of the greatness of Allah, based on His saying: ﴿taking retribution﴾, for the plural form here is for magnification.

**Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on Surah 32, verses 14–30 (part 6 of 7)**

* Among the benefits of this noble verse is the eloquence (balaghah) of the Qur'an, and that it is at the highest level of eloquence and clarity. This is seen in His saying: ﴿Indeed, from the criminals﴾, rather than saying "Indeed, from it" [i.e., from the criminals]. This gives two benefits. The first is that this (group) is criminal. The second is that the ruling applies to them and to other criminals.

Then He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And We had certainly given Moses the Book﴾ [Surah al-Sajdah 23], to the end.

* From this noble verse is derived the affirmation of Moses's prophethood, ﴿And We had certainly given Moses the Book﴾, and the emphasis on this prophethood through His saying ﴿And We had certainly given﴾. The sentence is emphasized with three emphatic particles: the lam, qad, and the implied oath.

* Among its benefits: Moses, peace be upon him, was truly a messenger, and there is no room for doubt about him, through His saying: ﴿So do not be in doubt about meeting him﴾ [Surah al-Sajdah 23]. That is, this is a truth; do not be in doubt that what happened to Moses did happen. This is according to the interpretation we mentioned. As for what the author (al-Mu'allif) said, it is derived from it that Muhammad ﷺ would meet Moses.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the Torah, like the Qur'an, is guidance. This is through His saying: ﴿And We made it guidance﴾, but it is specific guidance. For whom? For the Children of Israel: ﴿And We made it guidance for the Children of Israel﴾ [Surah al-Sajdah 23].

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: an indication that we should not seek guidance from the Torah. From where do we take it? From His saying: ﴿guidance for the Children of Israel﴾. As for those after the sending of the Messenger, their guidance is the Qur'an.

Then He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And We made from among them leaders guiding by Our command when they were patient and were certain of Our signs﴾ [Surah al-Sajdah 24], to the end.

* From this noble verse is derived the virtue of patience. From where do we derive the virtue of patience? From the reward for it, and from the fact that the patient person becomes a leader. This is evidence that patience is beloved to Allah, and He rewards it with this great reward.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the virtue of certainty (yaqin), as in His saying: ﴿and were certain of Our signs﴾.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: attaining leadership in religion through these two qualities, which are patience and certainty.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the reward is of the same kind as the deed. Because these people were patient and had certainty, they became leaders who are followed. Whenever a person is afflicted by something, he says: "So-and-so was afflicted and was patient," and he becomes patient. Whenever a doubt comes to him, he says: "So-and-so was certain," and so he becomes certain, and thereby the person becomes a leader.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of Allah's signs (ayat): ﴿and were certain of Our signs﴾.

He said: ﴿Indeed, your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that about which they used to differ﴾ [Surah al-Sajdah 25].

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: there is no judge in the Hereafter except Allah. From where is this taken? From the pronoun of separation (dhamir al-fasl, a pronoun used to emphasize exclusivity) in ﴿Indeed, your Lord, He is the one who will judge﴾. He alone judges. Allah, the Most High, has said in another verse: ﴿Whose is the dominion today? It is for Allah, the One, the Subduer﴾ [Surah Ghafir 16], and He said: ﴿So judgment belongs to Allah, the Most High, the Most Great﴾ [Surah Ghafir 12].

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of the Day of Resurrection, through His saying ﴿the Day of Resurrection﴾.

* Among its benefits: that Allah, may He be exalted, judges between believers and disbelievers on that Day. ﴿Indeed, your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that about which they used to differ﴾. He will say: "You are upon truth, and you are upon falsehood; these are for Paradise and these are for the Fire." Which of them is the victorious?

* A student: The believers.

* The Shaykh: The believers? Are you certain? Or are the disbelievers the victorious? No, not the majority. Which of them is victorious?

* A student: The one who prevails.

* The Shaykh: The one who prevails.

* A student: The believers.

* The Shaykh: The believers? What is the evidence?

* A student: (...).

* The Shaykh: No.

* A student: ﴿And Allah will never give the disbelievers a way over the believers﴾.

* The Shaykh: ﴿So Allah will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection, and Allah will never give the disbelievers a way over the believers﴾ [Surah al-Nisa' 141]. Look, a judge announces the ruling between two litigants and says: "You are the victorious one." He announces the ruling before the case. Is this permissible or not? Regarding the right of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, there is no doubt that it is permissible. So now we say: "We dispute with the disbelievers, and they will have no way over us." But if, for example, a case comes up in this world, and the judge comes and says: "Such-and-such's claim (...), and that one has no way over you," is that permissible or not? This is not permissible. Firstly, because the judge has not yet been presented with the case and does not know. Secondly, the litigant, usually, what does he mention? Does he mention the proof that is in his favor or the proof against him? Usually he mentions the proof in his favor, whether he intends to conceal his opponent's case, or he thinks that this will benefit him. Yes indeed.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: there is no harmony between believers and disbelievers (...). ﴿concerning that about which they used to differ﴾. Any person who tries to bring together Islam and Christianity, or Islam and Judaism, has wanted to return the milk to the udder. Is that possible or not? Is it possible or impossible? It is impossible. Every disbeliever, whoever he may be, whether he claims affiliation with Islam or is a disbeliever openly declaring his disbelief, can never be in harmony with the believers, never. Whoever claims otherwise has strayed far and attempted something impossible.

Then He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Has it not become clear to them how many generations We destroyed before them, [generations] in whose dwellings they walk? Indeed, in that are signs. Then will they not listen?﴾ [Surah al-Sajdah 26].

* From this noble verse is derived the use of parables (darb al-amthal). From where is this taken? From His saying: ﴿Has it not become clear to them how many We destroyed﴾. That is: if We destroyed those before them, then We will destroy them if they are like them. For this reason, Allah, the Most High, said in Surah Yusuf: ﴿There was certainly in their stories a lesson for those of understanding. It was not a narration invented, but a confirmation of what was before it and a detailed explanation of all things, and guidance and mercy for a people who believe﴾ [Surah Yusuf 111].

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: inferring the intelligible from the perceptible, through His saying: ﴿in whose dwellings they walk﴾. Or, in other words, inferring the "certainty of sight" ('ayn al-yaqin) from the truth of "certainty of knowledge" ('ilm al-yaqin). ﴿how many generations We destroyed before them﴾, what is this? It is "certainty of knowledge." ﴿in whose dwellings they walk﴾, this is "certainty of sight." Yes.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the permissibility of walking in the homes and dwellings of those who were punished. From where do we take it?

* A student: (...).

* The Shaykh: He said: ﴿in whose dwellings they walk﴾. Does the report of a thing indicate its permissibility?

* A student: Yes.

* The Shaykh: No. In reality it does not indicate that. The fact that they walk in their dwellings does not indicate that this walking is authorized. The Prophet, peace be upon him, reported: "Indeed, a woman (al-ẓa'īnah, a woman traveling alone on a camel) will travel from Hadramawt to Aden, or to San'a, fearing none but Allah"[[Narrated by al-Humaydi in his Musnad (940) from 'Adi ibn Hatim, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "How will you be when the woman travels from the farthest part of Yemen to the palaces of al-Hirah, fearing none but Allah." And al-Bukhari (3595) narrated from him, that Hatim said: While I was with the Prophet ﷺ, a man came to him and complained of poverty, then another came and complained of highway robbery. He said: "O 'Adi, have you seen al-Hirah?" I said: I have not seen it, but I have been informed about it. He said: "If you live long, you will see the woman travel from al-Hirah until she circles the Ka'bah, fearing no one but Allah..." The hadith.]]. And a woman alone, is that forbidden or not?

* A student: Yes.

* The Shaykh: It is forbidden. And the Messenger said: "You will certainly follow the ways of those before you"[[Narrated by Ahmad (21897) from the hadith of Abu Waqid al-Laythi, may Allah be pleased with him.]], the Jews and the Christians. Is this forbidden or permitted?

* A student: Forbidden.

* The Shaykh: Forbidden. So the report that they walk in their dwellings does not indicate that walking is permissible. But does it indicate that it is forbidden? It does not indicate that it is forbidden, nor that it is permissible. So we return to the evidences that indicate this, whether prohibition or permission, and we find that the evidences indicate that traveling through them is permissible, but residing in them is not permissible. Furthermore, the Messenger, peace be upon him, said: "Do not enter upon these punished people unless you are weeping. If you are not weeping, do not enter them"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (4702) and Muslim (2980/38) from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him.]]. Is it clear? So the person who intends to visit them, we say: do not enter them except weeping. As for one who passes through them in passing, he may pass, but he should hasten, as the Prophet, peace be upon him, hastened.

As for going to these dwellings for the purpose of sightseeing, saying: "Masha'Allah, by Allah, what a great civilization this is! Look at the ancient civilization. Is there a new civilization like it?" and his speech implies glorifying these people, this is from traveling in the land in a manner that is not commanded. Do you agree?

* Students: No.

* The Shaykh: We do not agree. This is from traveling in the land in a manner that is forbidden, because our entering upon these people to enjoy ourselves, amazed and dazzled by their power, forgetting the punishment that befell them for opposing the command of Allah and His messengers, is blameworthy, not praiseworthy, and not commanded. Accordingly, we say to everyone who wishes to go to these lands: if you did that for the sake of mere recreation, then it is forbidden for you. But if it is for the sake of reflection and admonition from what befell them of punishment and retribution, and that you be affected by it until you weep, then this is permissible. Otherwise, do not enter; do not expose yourselves to punishment.

* A student: Setting out on journeys (shadd al-rihal)?

* The Shaykh: Setting out on journeys is not a problem, because it is not for the purpose of worshipping that place itself.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that in the destruction of nations there is a lesson and a sign. This is through His saying: ﴿Indeed, in that are signs. Then will they not listen?﴾. It is a sign because Allah seized them and destroyed them despite their strength, and it is a lesson that Allah seized them. Why? Because of their opposition, as Allah, the Most High, said: ﴿Have they not traveled in the land and seen how was the end of those before them? They were greater than them in power and in traces left upon the earth, but Allah seized them for their sins﴾ [Surah Ghafir 21]. And He said in another verse: ﴿Then what availed them what they had earned?﴾ [Surah al-Hijr 84]. And He said in another verse: ﴿They were greater than them in power, and they plowed the earth and populated it more than they have populated it﴾ [Surah al-Rum 9]. All of this indicates that we are obligated to take lessons from these verses and to fear.

Then He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Have they not seen that We drive the water to dry land and bring forth thereby crops from which eat their livestock and themselves? Then will they not see?﴾ [Surah al-Sajdah 27], to the end.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the obligation to reflect upon the signs, because the interrogative here is for rebuke and for blaming those who did not benefit from it.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of Allah's voluntary actions (af'al ikhtiyariyyah): ﴿that We drive﴾.

* Among its benefits: the demonstration of the power of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in that He drives water, by air or by land, to these barren, dead, dry lands, so they grow; through His saying: ﴿to dry land, and We bring forth thereby crops﴾.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the basic ruling on what grows from the earth is permissibility (al-hill). From where is this taken? ﴿from which eat their livestock and themselves﴾. So the basic ruling on what grows from the earth is that it is permissible, until there is evidence of prohibition.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the demonstration of Allah's power in bringing the earth to life after its death: ﴿and We bring forth thereby crops from which eat their livestock and themselves﴾ [Surah al-Sajdah 27].

* Among its benefits: an indication of the highest degree of certainty, which is the "truth of certainty" (haqq al-yaqin). From where is this taken? From His saying: ﴿from which eat their livestock﴾. They do not merely look at it, but they eat from it, and this is the truth of certainty.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: encouragement to reflect and to observe. From where is this taken? From His saying: ﴿Then will they not see?﴾ [Surah al-Sajdah 27].

* Among its benefits: the affirmation of ownership over livestock, through His saying ﴿their livestock﴾. The attribution here is an attribution of ownership. But it has already been mentioned to us that every ownership a person has is ownership belonging to Allah; however, it is restricted ownership. A person does not own a thing with absolute ownership to dispose of as he wishes. Rather, he owns it with restricted ownership: in acquiring it, in developing it (tamwil, i.e., trading with it), and in disposing of it. Is that correct or not? It is restricted in acquisition: you do not acquire it except in a legitimate way. In its development, meaning trading with it. And in its disposal: you do not dispose of it except in a restricted manner. So after this, is ownership real or truly absolute? No.

Accordingly, your ownership of things, even your private property such as a house, a car, or a garment, is not absolute ownership. Rather, it is restricted ownership.

Then He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And they say, "When is this victory, if you should be truthful?"﴾ [Surah al-Sajdah 28]. In this is evidence of the foolishness and folly of these deniers, through their saying ﴿When is this victory, if you should be truthful?﴾. We have said that the interrogative here expresses impatience and a challenge to the Messenger, peace be upon him, and to those with him.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the judgment between the believer and the disbeliever is a "victory" (fath). Because Allah said: ﴿Say, "On the Day of Victory, no benefit will the faith of those who disbelieved be"﴾ [Surah al-Sajdah 29], so He affirmed this name.

* Among the benefits of this verse: the demonstration of the arrogance ('utuww) and criminality of the disbelievers, because they challenge the Messenger, peace be upon him, and the believers, saying: "When is this judgment between us, if you are truthful?"

* Among the benefits of the verse that follows: that when punishment descends, faith does not benefit. From where is this derived? ﴿Say, "On the Day of Victory, no benefit will the faith of those who disbelieved be"﴾ [Surah al-Sajdah 29].

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that when punishment descends, there is no respite: ﴿nor will they be reprieved﴾.

* Among its benefits: that punishment may be postponed before it descends. Is that so? Yes, because He says: ﴿On the Day of Victory, no benefit will be [faith]﴾. The apparent meaning of the verse is that if this faith occurred before the punishment descended, then Allah, may He be exalted, would accept it. This is why the Prophet, peace be upon him, at the eclipse, commanded what? Prayer, supplication, seeking forgiveness, charity, and glorifying Allah (takbir), so that the punishment that this eclipse warns of might be lifted. Indeed, the eclipse is a warning of punishment; it is not itself punishment, but it is a warning that creation may be punished. When they turn to prayer, remembrance, supplication, and seeking forgiveness, it is lifted from them.

Then He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿So turn away from them and wait; indeed, they are [also] waiting﴾ [Surah al-Sajdah 30].

* From the noble verse is derived: the obstinate person (al-mukabir) should be turned away from and left until punishment descends upon him. So if you see someone who is obstinate, you command him with the truth, but he is obstinate, argues, and opposes, then leave him, because your remaining with him is of no use. The obstinate person who says: "This is not the sun, rather it is the moon," and you say: "Now we are in the day, at midmorning, look at the sun," and he says: "No, you are mistaken; we are now after the 'Isha' prayer, and what you see is only the moon," do you speak with him? Never. You seek someone to recite over him or to treat him, because he is insane. Likewise, the one to whom you show the truth as clearly as the sun, and the truth is clearer than the sun, yet he says: "No, this is not correct." He should be sought someone to treat his mind before his thinking. This is an obstinate person with whom there is no benefit in speaking. For this reason, the poet says:

How can a thing be established in minds
when daylight itself needs proof?

Among the benefits of this noble verse: the one who denies, what does he await for his denial? He awaits nothing but punishment: ﴿Indeed, they are awaiting﴾. As for the author's explanation, that ﴿they are awaiting﴾ means that some destruction or the like will befall you, this is open to question. Rather, it is said that they are awaiting punishment by virtue of their having persisted in their disbelief, so they are like one who waits for what is about to descend upon them.

It may also be said that the verse includes both meanings together: they await (...) that you die, and they await their punishment by their persistence in disobedience, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Or do they say, "A poet, for whom we await the misfortunes of time." Say, "Wait, for I am with you among those who wait."﴾ [at-Tur 30–31], and ﴿So wait, indeed they are waiting﴾ [as-Sajdah 30]. We ask Allah for well-being.

* A student: Is al-intizar (waiting) the same as at-taraqqub (watching expectantly)?
* The Shaykh: Yes, indeed, at-taraqqub.
* The student: It is said: they await a painful punishment.
* The Shaykh: Yes, how? They await it, whether they perceive it or not, because their final destination is punishment, and we seek refuge in Allah. For this reason, when the disbeliever dies he is punished continuously; indeed, he senses the punishment at the time of death agony: ﴿until, when death comes to one of them, he says, "My Lord, send me back, that I may do righteousness in what I have left behind."﴾ [al-Mu'minun 99–100]. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿No! It is but a word he is saying, and behind them is a barrier until the Day they are resurrected.﴾ [al-Mu'minun 100]

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 32, verse 14–30 (part 1 of 7):

Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: ﴿So taste [the punishment] for your forgetting the meeting of this your Day; indeed, We have forgotten you﴾ [As-Sajdah 14].

The author says: (The guardians will say to them when they enter it: ﴿So taste [the punishment] for your forgetting﴾.) Let us consider the author's words and see whether they agree with the apparent meaning of the verse. We read: ﴿So taste [the punishment] for your forgetting the meeting of this your Day; indeed, We have forgotten you.﴾ Is it appropriate that the speaker be the angels, and that the angels say: ﴿indeed, We have forgotten you﴾?
* Student: No.
* The Shaykh: Who then is the speaker? Allah, yes, as He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿They forgot Allah, so He forgot them﴾ [At-Tawbah 67].
The correct view is that this statement is the speech of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. He says it to them as reproach, rebuke and also humiliation. He says: ﴿So taste [the punishment] for your forgetting﴾. The command here is not (...), nor is it a mere command, but it is for rebuke, reproach and disgrace.
﴿So taste for your forgetting the meeting of this your Day﴾. The author said: (So taste the punishment). This interpretation informs us that the object of (taste) is omitted; its estimated object is "the punishment." It is also possible that it has no object, and the meaning is like His saying: ﴿Taste! Indeed, you are the mighty, the noble﴾ [Ad-Dukhan 49], so the intended meaning is merely rebuke and humiliation.
He says: (﴿So taste for your forgetting the meeting of this your Day﴾, i.e., because of your abandoning belief in it and working for it). By his words "because of your abandoning" he informs us that (ma) is a verbal-source particle (mas­dariyyah), and that (nasītum) means (tarakatum, you abandoned). This is correct, for (ma) is verbal-source, meaning "for your forgetting," and forgetting here means abandonment, not the forgetting that is the heart's lapse from a known matter. For the familiar forgetting is the heart's lapse from something known, and for this a person is not punished. Forgetting is also applied to abandonment, and this is what one is punished for.

The evidence that forgetting is applied to abandonment is His saying: ﴿They forgot Allah, so He forgot them﴾ [At-Tawbah 67]. And this verse, ﴿indeed, We have forgotten you﴾ [As-Sajdah 14], means "We have abandoned you." It does not mean the heart's lapse from a known matter, as in His saying: ﴿In a Book; my Lord neither errs nor forgets﴾ [Ta-Ha 52]. The forgetting negated of Allah is different from the forgetting affirmed of Him: the affirmed forgetting is abandonment, and the negated forgetting is the lapse from a thing.

﴿for your forgetting the meeting of this your Day﴾ [As-Sajdah 14]: (nasītum) means "you abandoned its meeting," you abandoned the meeting; the intended meaning is that you abandoned working for it and believing in it.

﴿indeed, We have forgotten you﴾ [As-Sajdah 14]: We have abandoned you in the punishment – we ask Allah for well-being – Allah, Mighty and Majestic, abandoned them. He did not forget them; He still knows of them, Exalted is He, but He abandoned them. He said to them, after the reply: ﴿Be silent therein, and do not speak to Me﴾ [Al-Mu'minun 108]. Do they speak after that inside the punishment? Never, because in the Hereafter they are unable to oppose Him once He has said: ﴿Be silent therein, and do not speak to Me.﴾ Their hope is cut off from every hope – we seek refuge in Allah – yes, and they despair of every good.

(﴿indeed, We have forgotten you﴾: We have abandoned you in the punishment. ﴿And taste the punishment of eternity﴾: the lasting one. ﴿For what you used to do﴾: of disbelief and denial.) This is an affirmation of certainty and a clarification that what they have tasted cannot be removed from them, even though they said earlier: ﴿Return us, and we will act righteously﴾ [As-Sajdah 12], and He said: there is no return.

﴿And taste the punishment of eternity﴾ means the lasting punishment. This is from the attribution of a thing to its kind, or the preposition (fi, in) is taken as indicating location: a punishment in eternity. In any case, it is a lasting punishment.

﴿the punishment of eternity for what you used to do﴾: (ma) here may be a relative pronoun, meaning "for that which you used to do in the world," and it may be verbal-source. But the apparent sense of the author's explanation is that it is a relative pronoun: (﴿for what you used to do﴾: of disbelief and denial).

Then Allah, Exalted is He, clarified who is truly a believer, saying: (﴿Those who believe in Our verses﴾: the Qur'an ﴿are those who, when they are reminded of them﴾ [As-Sajdah 15]). (Innama) is a particle of restriction; it restricts belief to whom? To those who, when reminded of the verses of their Lord, fall down in prostration.

His saying: ﴿Only those believe in Our verses﴾: the author said: (the Qur'an). On this basis, they are the legislated verses. The correct view is that it is general, including the cosmic verses. Whoever is reminded of what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, does to the deniers and the criminals, that falls within the words ﴿Our verses﴾.

His saying "the Qur'an" implies that this statement is specific to this community, ﴿Only those believe in Our verses﴾, because they are the people of the Qur'an. But it is better to take it in a general sense, even regarding what came before: ﴿Indeed, those who were given knowledge before it, when it is recited to them, fall down prostrate on their chins﴾ [Al-Isra' 107].

He says: ﴿Only those believe in Our verses who, when they are reminded of them﴾ [As-Sajdah 15]. (Alladhina) – what is its i'rab?
(Alladhina) is the subject (fa'il) of (yu'minu), meaning: none believe except those who... and the intended belief is complete belief.

His saying: (﴿Those who, when they are reminded﴾: are admonished ﴿by them﴾): i.e., they were made an admonition for them, and the verses were explained to them. When they are admonished by them, ﴿they fall down prostrate﴾. (Kharrū, they fell) is the answer of (idha, when). ﴿They fell down prostrate.﴾ Falling (kharur) happens from a higher place to a lower one, and from it comes the falling of water (...) from above to below.

﴿They fell down prostrate﴾ from standing. ﴿And glorified the praise of their Lord﴾ while prostrating ﴿and they are not arrogant﴾ [As-Sajdah 15].

Some scholars raised a difficulty concerning this verse and said: Does everyone who is reminded of Allah's verses prostrate, or what? Are you now saying that a person is not a believer unless, when the verse is recited to him, he prostrates, or when you admonish him with an admonition, he prostrates? That is not so.

So what is the answer to this verse?

Some of them said: the meaning is ﴿when they are reminded by them, they fall down prostrate﴾ at the place of prostration; that is, if a verse of prostration passes by them, they prostrate, but if they are reminded of their Lord's verses without a verse of prostration passing by them, they do not prostrate. But the correct view is otherwise. The correct view is that the meaning is: those who, when they are reminded by them, submit to them and humble themselves before them. It does not follow that the prostration must be immediate upon the reminder. ﴿When they are reminded by them, they fall down prostrate﴾ means even in the future, so the answer need not be immediately connected to the condition; that is, the answer of the conditional need not follow directly upon it.

What the sequence-indicating letters or the construction imply may be intended as sequence in its place, in each matter according to its nature. Thus, if you say: "Zayd married, then a child was born to him" – the fa' indicates sequence and immediacy – and it is known that a child is not born to him merely upon the contract of marriage. Is that not so, or not? Reflect: is a child born to him the moment the marriage contract is concluded?
* Students: No.
* The Shaykh: So the fa' indicates sequence and immediacy; we say: immediacy in each thing according to its nature. And Allah, Exalted is He, said: ﴿Have you not seen that Allah sends down water from the sky, and the earth becomes green?﴾ [Al-Hajj 63]. When the rain falls, does the earth become green in the morning? No, but after a period it turns green, and after a period a child is born to that married man. Likewise here: ﴿When they are reminded by them, they fall down﴾ does not mean that mere reminding makes them prostrate; rather the meaning is that they commit to it. When they are reminded by them, they commit to it in hearing and obedience, so they prostrate at the place of prostration and no arrogance is found in them. On this basis, there is no difficulty in the verse.

﴿They fell down prostrate﴾: (sujjadan, prostrating) is a circumstantial accusative (hal) from the subject of (kharru), and ﴿and glorified﴾ is conjoined to (kharru). The meaning of (sabbahu) is "they declared Him free of imperfection." Its object is omitted; the estimate: "they glorified their Lord" or "they glorified Allah."

His saying: (accompanied by ﴿the praise of their Lord﴾): the author informed us that the (ba') in His saying ﴿with the praise of their Lord﴾ is the ba' of accompaniment, meaning that the glorification is joined with praise. Yet if he had gone to the view that the ba' is for accompaniment, and "they glorified with a glorification accompanied by the praise of their Lord," it would have been better.

(﴿And glorified the praise of their Lord﴾: i.e., they said: "Glory be to Allah and by His praise.") This is the meaning of "glorified with the praise of their Lord": they said, "Glory be to Allah and by His praise." It is possible that the intended glorification and praise are not of the tongue alone, but that they declared Him free of what is unfitting with their hearts and praised Him with their tongues: they declared Him free of what is unfitting with their hearts and praised Him with their tongues with what He deserves.

﴿And they are not arrogant﴾ [As-Sajdah 15]: the clause is a circumstantial clause; that is, while they are not arrogant against belief and obedience, but they submit and humble themselves.

Then Allah, Exalted is He, mentioned from their attributes what He mentioned in His saying: (﴿Their sides forsake their beds﴾ [As-Sajdah 16]: they rise and also withdraw), for (mujafah) means separation. From it: "The Prophet ﷺ used to hold his elbows away from his sides in prostration"[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (828) and Ibn Majah (1061), whose wording it is, from the hadith of Abu Humayd al-Sa'idi.]], meaning he keeps them away from his sides. So its meaning is separation and rising, and rising entails distance.

﴿from the beds﴾ [As-Sajdah 16]: "al-madaji'" is the plural of "madja'," the place of lying down, and lying down is sleep. The author says: (the places of lying down with their bedding, for their prayer at night in tahajjud). They do not sleep: their sides forsake their beds, so they do not sleep. But this is restricted by what the Sunnah has brought: that they perform tahajjud, not the whole night, but the time legislated for tahajjud.

(﴿They call upon their Lord in fear﴾: of His punishment ﴿and in hope﴾: of His mercy): ("they call upon") is a circumstantial clause from the subject of (tatajafa) or from the possessive pronoun in (junubuhum); that is, while they call upon their Lord.

Is the supplication a request, or worship, or both? It includes both: they call upon Him with supplication of request and of worship.

﴿their Lord in fear and hope﴾: fear of Allah's punishment, Mighty and Majestic, and hope for His mercy. But what drives fear and hope? When they look at their shortcomings and the greatness of Allah and the severity of His punishment, the side of fear prevails over them; and when they look at the vastness of Allah's mercy and His pardon, and that they have done what they should do, the side of hope prevails over them. They travel with two wings: the wing of fear and the wing of hope.

But which of them should be given precedence? There is no disagreement: Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, said: his fear and his hope should be balanced; whichever prevails, his companion is ruined, for if he prevails with the side of fear he despairs of Allah's mercy, and if he prevails with the side of hope he feels safe from Allah's plan, but it should be between the two.

He says: the sound view is to give precedence to the side of fear, and the sick person gives precedence to the side of hope; that is, at the time of sickness he gives precedence to the side of hope and expectation, while in health he gives precedence to the side of fear.

It was also said: if he performs an act of obedience, let him give precedence to the side of hope, and if he intends sin or commits it, let him give precedence to the side of fear.

(﴿And from what We have provided them they spend﴾ [As-Sajdah 16]: they give charity.) Is the (min) here for specifying the kind, or is it partitive: some of what We provided them they spend?
* Student: The first.
* Another student: Partitive.
* The Shaykh: Partitive. If you say it is partitive, then whoever gives all his wealth seeking nearness to Allah becomes blameworthy. If you say it specifies the kind, and they spend from what We provided them, then it does not require that whoever spends all his wealth be blameworthy, because the intended meaning is specifying the kind, which includes the whole, the little and the much.

This matter is one on which the scholars differed: does a person spend all his wealth in obedience to Allah and in the way of Allah, or does he limit himself to part of it?

The correct view is that this depends on the person's condition and on the means by which he保 averts necessity from himself and his family. If a person is weak in reliance on Allah or weak in ability to earn, then it is better that he spend a portion of his wealth. If the matter is the reverse, he may give away all his wealth in charity, as Abu Bakr did. As for Abu Lubabah, when he vowed to strip himself of his wealth as charity to Allah and His Messenger, the Messenger ﷺ said to him: "Keep some of your wealth for yourself, for it is better for you."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (2757) from the hadith of Ka'b ibn Malik.]] So he made it good for him to keep some of the wealth.

His saying: ﴿they spend﴾: spending is giving.

Allah, Exalted is He, said: ﴿No soul knows what is hidden for them of comfort for the eyes, as a reward for what they used to do﴾ [As-Sajdah 17]. "No soul knows": any soul at all, neither an honoured angel nor a sent prophet, does not know ﴿what is hidden for them of comfort for the eyes.﴾ This is a negation of knowledge of the reality, not of knowledge of the meaning, for the meaning is known through what Allah has informed of comfort for the eyes, but the reality of that thing is unknown.

Hence Ibn 'Abbas said: "There is nothing in this world of what is in Paradise except the names."[[Narrated by al-Bayhaqi in al-Ba'th wa al-Nushur (332).]] It is known that in Paradise there are palm trees, pomegranates, fruit, milk, honey, water, wine, birds and the like; we know this, and we know the meaning, but the reality of that thing is unknown, is it not? It is unknown. ﴿No soul knows what is hidden for them﴾: i.e., the reality of what is hidden; the meaning of what is hidden is not the issue, the meaning is known.

His saying: (﴿of comfort for the eyes﴾ [As-Sajdah 17]: what delights their eyes). "Qarrat 'aynuhu" means it became cool, and "qarrat 'aynuhu" also means it became settled. On the first meaning it derives from qurr, which is cold; hence it is said that the tear of joy is cold and the tear of sorrow is hot, and so he says: "qarrat 'aynuhu" when he is pleased. As for if it derives from qarar, meaning that they do not look to anything other than what they are looking at – that is, their eyes are settled and do not turn to anything other than what they are in – both meanings are correct: "qarrat 'aynuhu" means it cooled, so no heat of sorrow reaches it; and "qarrat 'aynuka" means it settled, so it does not look at anything other than what it is on, and this signifies the utmost of desire.

The author said: (And in one reading, with a sukun on the yā' of the present tense.) What is the sukun on the yā'? (ukhfiya) is a past verb; (ukhfī) is a present verb, or not? Ukhfī means "I."
﴿No soul knows what is hidden for them﴾: what is hidden for them, I (Allah, Mighty and Majestic) ﴿of comfort for the eyes﴾ [As-Sajdah 17]. But ﴿what is hidden for them﴾ is a past verb in the passive voice, and its subject is concealed: is it obligatorily or permissibly concealed? If it is (ukhfiya), it is concealed...
* Student: Obligatorily.
* The Shaykh: No, permissibly. If it is (ukhfiya), it is a past verb with a permissibly concealed subject; if it is (ukhfī) with a sukun, it is a present verb with an obligatorily concealed subject, whose estimate is: "I."

The meaning is correct on both readings, for Allah is the One who concealed it, even with the passive form ﴿what is hidden﴾, since the one who conceals is Allah: ﴿what is hidden for them of comfort for the eyes﴾ [As-Sajdah 17].

He said: ﴿as a reward for what they used to do﴾ [As-Sajdah 17]: (jaza'an) is an object of purpose (maf'ul li-ajlihi), but is its governing verb (ukhfiya) or (qurrah)? The apparent view is that it is (qurrah): their eyes are cooled as a reward, and the meaning is not "it was concealed for them as a reward"; for it might be said that the manifestation is more eloquent as a reward, but it is "of comfort for the eyes, as a reward."

﴿as a reward for what they used to do﴾ [As-Sajdah 17]: i.e., for what they used to do in the world of obedience to Allah. If you say: this indicates that they are rewarded for their deeds, and it has been established from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "No one will enter Paradise by his deeds." They said: "Not even you, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Not even I, unless Allah covers me with His mercy."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (6463) and Muslim (2816/71) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]] So what is the reconciliation between this hadith and this verse and its like?

The scholars said: the reconciliation between them is by the difference in the meaning of the (ba'). The ba' that indicates causation is the one found in such a verse as ﴿as a reward for what they used to do﴾, meaning: because of what they used to do.

The letter bāʾ (ب) that expresses exchange is the one mentioned in His words: ﴿No one will enter Paradise because of his deeds﴾, meaning in exchange for his deeds. This is because if we intended exchange and equivalence, the worker would appear shortchanged. Is he or is he not? If we intended equivalence and exchange, then whatever righteous deeds the worker performs, he would still owe something, since one single blessing among the blessings of God upon him would cover all his deeds. For example, someone says: "Praise be to God, I pray the five prayers, fast Ramadan, pay the zakat on my wealth, and perform the Hajj to the House." Is this a rank that earns Paradise, yes or no? If we wanted to match it against one of God's blessings...

And His words: ﴿Is one who is a believer like one who is defiant? They are not equal﴾ [As-Sajdah 18]. The defiance meant here is the major defiance that takes one out of Islam, not the minor defiance by which a person remains a believer with deficient faith.

﴿Like one who is defiant﴾. The answer is ﴿They are not equal﴾. Reader, pay attention and pause at His words ﴿defiant﴾, because many readers recite and continue: ﴿Is one who is a believer like one who is defiant, they are not equal﴾, which is not correct. ﴿Like one who is defiant, they are not equal﴾ is not sound. So pause at ﴿defiant﴾, then say: ﴿They are not equal﴾. Whose answer is this? It is the answer of God, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿They are not equal.﴾ God, exalted is He, posed the question and answered it Himself: ﴿Is one who is a believer like one who is defiant?﴾ He answered: ﴿They are not equal﴾ (meaning the believers and the defiant). Why?

(...) (﴿As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, for them are the Gardens of Refuge as a lodging﴾ [As-Sajdah 19], which is what is prepared for a guest, ﴿for what they used to do﴾.) ﴿As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, then for them﴾. The word ʾammā (أمّا) here is a conditional and detailing particle, and along with the condition and detail it conveys emphasis. Compare: ﴿As for he who gives and fears God, and affirms the best [reward], We will ease him toward ease﴾ [Al-Layl 5–7], and ﴿As for he who withholds and considers himself self-sufficient, and denies the best [reward], We will ease him toward hardship﴾ [Al-Layl 8–10].

Here, in ﴿As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, then for them the Gardens of Refuge﴾, there are three benefits:
Conditional: as evidenced by the fact that it is followed by an answer, ﴿then for them﴾.
Detailing: because it introduces two categories, ﴿As for those who believed﴾ and ﴿And as for those who defied﴾. What comes next?
Emphatic: because there is no doubt that this structure conveys emphasis. ﴿As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, then for them﴾ is the protasis, and ﴿then for them the Gardens of Refuge﴾ is the apodosis.

The word jannāt is the plural of jannah, which linguistically means a garden with many trees. It was so named because it covers those within it, meaning it conceals them. In the Sharia, however, it is the abode God has prepared for His friends, and it is higher than anything imagined or occurring to the mind.

His words ﴿the Gardens of Refuge﴾ mean the gardens that are their abode, where they desire no change and do not turn away from them. It is a refuge just as Hellfire is the refuge of the disbelievers, who do not turn away from it. Thus "refuge" (maʾwā) is the place of lodging, meaning these are their gardens, where they take shelter and from which they do not depart.

﴿Lodging﴾: The author says it is what is prepared for a guest. Accordingly, it is a verbal noun in the accusative of state, meaning that this lodging is prepared for them.

﴿For what they used to do﴾: the bāʾ here indicates causation.

(﴿And as for those who defied﴾, through disbelief and denial, ﴿then their refuge is the Fire﴾, may God protect us. Their refuge, meaning their return, is ﴿the Fire﴾. Do they come out of it? No. ﴿Every time they wish to get out of it, they will be returned into it﴾. We seek refuge in God. Notice: ﴿every time they wish to get out of it﴾. They are given hope of leaving, and they are raised up until they approach its gates. Then, after they hope to leave and desire it, they are sent back into it. This is, may God protect us, more severe in punishment, is it not? If you were imprisoned in a place and someone said to you, "Come, come," and then when you approached the door, he turned you back, which is worse: that you remain in the cell, or this? Is remaining in the cell worse? Which is more severe?)

Student: The first.

Shaykh: Yes, indeed. Being brought close to the door, then when he wants to leave, being told, "Go back," because, may God protect us, when this is done, it is as if he is imprisoned several times. For one who has approached life and then returns to death, that becomes a second death, so returning him to his prison is a second imprisonment. Thus are the people of the Fire, may God protect us: they are given hope of leaving, and every time they wish to leave, they are returned into it.

﴿And it will be said to them﴾ also as a rebuke: ﴿And it will be said to them, "Taste the punishment of the Fire which you used to deny."﴾ So they are gathered together, may God protect us, in both physical punishment and heart-felt punishment. The physical: from the Fire, may God protect us: ﴿Every time their skins are roasted through, We will replace them with other skins﴾ [An-Nisa 56]. The heart-felt: from this rebuke, ﴿Taste the punishment of the Fire which you used to deny﴾. What is a person's regret when told such a thing? Does he not feel remorse and say, "I wish I had not denied"? How could I deny? He wishes so. This, may God protect us, contains rebuke, reproach, and the infliction of regret, which is evident. For this reason, He, glorified and exalted, said in another verse: ﴿Thus will God show them their deeds as regrets for them, and they will never get out of the Fire﴾ [Al-Baqarah 167]. Now, if something we desire is missed by the decree and destiny of God, does one feel regret? One regrets, saying: "If only I had done this, if only I had done that." Even though this is forbidden, because it opens the door to Satan's work, opens the door to regret or objecting to destiny. For this reason the Messenger (ﷺ) forbade it.

So the point is that this rebuke becomes a punishment of the heart. As for their repeated saying, ﴿every time they wish to get out of it, they are returned into it﴾, this is physical, bodily punishment. They are, may God protect us, perpetual in punishment, regret, and remorse: ﴿Their punishment will not be lightened for them, and they will be in it in despair﴾ [Az-Zukhruf 75]. Always and forever there is no respite. For this reason they say: ﴿Those in the Fire will say to the keepers of Hell, "Call upon your Lord to lighten for us one day of the punishment"﴾ [Ghafir 49]. Note, may God protect us, the humiliation and the lowliness: they did not say "call your Lord to remove the punishment"; they said "lighten," only, and not "lighten always," but "lighten one day." This shows the intensity of their despair, because they have been despaired of mercy, may God protect us. They wish, yet they have no standing before God to request, so they ask the keepers of Hell to intercede with God to lighten it for them: ﴿lighten﴾, not remove; ﴿one day﴾, not always: ﴿lighten for us one day of the punishment﴾.

But what do the keepers say to them? They rebuke them: ﴿Did not your messengers come to you with clear proofs?﴾ [Ghafir 50]. They say, "Yes," ﴿They said, "Yes."﴾ Then they say, "Then we are free of you, we will not interfere in your affair," ﴿So call [upon Him yourselves]﴾ [Ghafir 50]. Call upon Him yourselves. God, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿And the supplication of the disbelievers is only in error﴾ [Ghafir 50], lost and of no benefit to them. For this reason, when they insist upon their Lord: ﴿Our Lord, our wretchedness overcame us, and we were a people astray. Our Lord, bring us out of it﴾ [Al-Muminun 106–107]. Note the humility in "Our Lord," and the acknowledgment in "our wretchedness overcame us," and "we were a people astray." They judged themselves, and all of this is from the category of humbling oneself, because when a person apologizes for his wrongdoing, this is a reason for mercy. If someone comes to you apologizing for his sin and admitting his sin, this obliges you to show him mercy. So they acknowledge, perhaps they will be shown mercy: ﴿Our Lord, bring us out of it, and if we return [to disbelief], then indeed we are wrongdoers﴾ [Al-Muminun 107]. God, exalted is He, says: ﴿Remain in it and do not speak to Me﴾. ﴿Remain in it﴾ means be humiliated and be abased, and ﴿do not speak to Me﴾ means not with any word at that time, may God protect us. They despair of every good. We ask God for safety. For this reason He said: ﴿And it will be said to them, "Taste the punishment of the Fire which you used to deny." And We will surely make them taste the nearer punishment short of the greater punishment﴾ [As-Sajdah 20–21]. This is a verb emphasized with the nūn and the lām: ﴿And We will surely make them taste﴾. Is it obligatory emphasis? It is obligatory emphasis, because it is affirmative, future, in answer to an oath, and [the lām] is used.)

﴿And We will surely make them taste the nearer punishment﴾: the punishment of this world, by killing, captivity, drought, years of famine, and diseases.

(﴿Short of the greater punishment﴾, meaning before ﴿the greater punishment﴾, which is the punishment of the Hereafter. ﴿So that they may return﴾, meaning whoever remains of them, ﴿may return﴾ to faith.) This is a warning from God, Mighty and Majestic, that He will make them taste the nearer punishment before the greater punishment, which is the punishment of the Hereafter, so that perhaps they will return. The particle "perhaps" (laʿalla, لعل) indicates causation. But did they return? Some of them returned and some did not. The Quraysh were struck with drought, years of famine, and killing at Badr, the killing of their nobles, and captivity as well. Did they return despite this? Some returned and some did not. Whoever God wills for salvation, God revives his heart through these admonitions, and he returns. Whoever God has sealed his heart upon remains as he is and does not return.

* * *

(﴿And who is more unjust than one who was reminded of the verses of his Lord﴾, the Qur'an, ﴿then turned away from them﴾, meaning there is no one more unjust than him.) ﴿Indeed, We will take retribution upon the criminals﴾ (﴿upon the criminals﴾, meaning the polytheists, ﴿We will take retribution﴾).

﴿And who is more unjust﴾: the author informed us by saying "there is no one more unjust" that the interrogative here is for negation, meaning no one is more unjust than him. Injustice (ẓulm) has been mentioned to us several times as meaning, in origin, deficiency. As in His words: ﴿Each of the two gardens yielded its produce and did not fall short therein at all﴾ [Al-Kahf 33], meaning it did not diminish. So its meaning is a person's deficiency in what is obligatory upon him, so he abandons it. That is, deficiency in what he is forbidden from, so he does not heed it and commits what is prohibited.

His words ﴿one who was reminded of the verses of his Lord﴾: He did not say "one whom the Messenger (ﷺ) reminded," so that it would include every reminder, because some people submit to certain reminders because of who the speaker is. Such a person does not submit to the verses; he submits to individuals. You find that if someone is reminded of this verse by a particular person, he accepts, and if another reminds him, he does not accept. Is that not so? There are people who, when someone commands them to a good matter, pay no attention and may even mock him, but when another commands the same thing, they comply and show agreement. For this reason He said "one who was reminded," so as not to restrict it to a specific reminder, whoever the reminder may be.

His words ﴿the verses of his Lord﴾: the author said the intended meaning is the Qur'an. The more correct view is that it is more general than the Qur'an, and includes even those who were reminded by the Torah in the time of the Torah, those reminded by the Gospel in the time of the Gospel, and by the Psalms in the time of the Psalms, because this is a general ruling.

His words ﴿the verses of his Lord﴾ mention Lordship (rubūbiyyah), which necessitates submission, because as long as he is reminded by the verses of a lord over him, you are a servant who is owned, and the one who is owned is under the management of whom? His lord.

﴿Then turned away from them﴾. In another verse: ﴿so turned away from it﴾ [Al-Kahf 57]. The difference is that in the other verse, ﴿so turned away﴾ means he hastened to turn away. In this verse, ﴿then turned away﴾ means after he reflected and considered the verse, he turned away. People are like this: some turn away at first glance and do not pay attention or reflect, and some may reflect but in the end turn away.

His words ﴿Indeed, We will take retribution upon the criminals﴾: the sentence is a resumptive sentence to threaten these turners-away and to explain that they are among the criminals. For this reason He said ﴿Indeed, We will take retribution upon the criminals﴾, which is an explicit noun in place of a pronoun. The original would be "Indeed, We will take retribution upon them," but the explicit noun was used in place of the pronoun for the two reasons mentioned earlier: so that a judgment of criminality is passed upon these people, and so that the ruling is general for every criminal among them and among others. Criminality (ijrām) means sin, so the criminal is the sinner who committed what is not lawful for him, as in His words: ﴿Indeed, those who committed crimes used to laugh at those who believed﴾ [Al-Mutaffifin 29].

He said ﴿Indeed, We will take retribution upon the criminals﴾. The word ﴿will take retribution﴾ is plural to agree with the subject. Where is the subject? "We" (innā), which is the subject of "innа" (inna), because its original form is "innanā," but the second nūn was dropped for lightness. ﴿Indeed, We will take retribution upon the criminals﴾. The plural here, and in everything attributed to God, is used to express majesty.
